of.needed: whether issuer signing keys (e.g. CA keys held in Secrets) are 3072-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys

consequence.statement: Signatures made with 3072-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys now use SHA-384 or SHA-512 instead of SHA-256. Upstream expects minimal impact and knows of no environments that break, but users of larger RSA keys should be aware of the change.
consequence.remediation: If you use 3072-bit or 4096-bit RSA keys, check that the systems consuming these certificates accept SHA-384 and SHA-512 signatures.

assertion.statement: In cert-manager v1.17.0, RSA signatures no longer always use SHA-256: the hash now depends on the RSA key length, with SHA-384 for 3072-bit keys and SHA-512 for 4096-bit keys.
